AGENDA
CITY OF AZUSA
REGULAR MEETING
OF THE CITY COUNCIL,
THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO
THE FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY, AND
THE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
AZUSA AUDITORIUM
213 EAST FOOTHILL BOULEVARD
AZUSA, CA 91702
MONDAY, APRIL 18, 2016
06:00 P.M.
Ceremonial/ Closed Session
Regular Meeting
AZUSA CITY COUNCIL
JOSEPH ROMERO ROCHA
MAYOR
ANGEL A. CARRILLO
MAYOR PRO TEM
EDWARD J. ALVAREZ
COUNCIL MEMBER
ROBERT GONZALES
COUNCIL MEMBER
URIEL E. MACIAS
COUNCIL MEMBER
06:00 P.M.
1.
Call to Order
2.
Roll Call
CLOSED SESSION
NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR CLOSED SESSION
Prior to going into closed session the City Council will convene in the Auditorium serving as Council Chambers to take public comment on the closed session items only. General public comment will be provided for during the regular portion of the meeting beginning at 7:30 P.M.
1.
CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS Pursuant to California Government Code, Section 54956.8. Property Address: 340 N. Orange Avenue (Azusa Armory)
Agency Negotiator: Troy Butzlaff, City Manager
Negotiating Parties: Daniel C. Kim, California Director of General Services
Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Sale
2.
CONFERENCE INVOLVING A JOINT POWERS AUTHORITY â€“ EAST SAN GABRIEL VALLEY CONSORTIUM dba L.A. WORKS Pursuant to California Government Code, Section 54956.96. Discussion will concern: Exposure to Litigation
Azusa Agency Representatives: Joe Rocha, Mayor; Troy Butzlaff, City Manager
3.
PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATIONS Pursuant to California Government Code, Section 54957. Titles: City Manager and City Attorney
7:30 P.M. - REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR REGULAR MEETING
Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection at the City Library.
Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the City Council meeting. When called, each person may address any item on or off the agenda during the public participation.
In compliance with Government code Section 54957.5, copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk - 213 E. Foothill Blvd.; copies for public view are at the Azusa City Library - 729 N. Dalton Ave., Azusa Police Department Lobby - 725 N. Alameda Ave., and the City of Azusa Web Page www.ci.azusa.ca.us. Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda or on a Public Hearing item, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to 7:30 P.M.; cards submitted after will not be accepted.
A.
PRELIMINARY BUSINESS
1.
Call to Order
2.
Roll Call
3.
Flag Salute
4.
Invocation â€“ Pastor Ariel Verayo, Jesus is Lord Church
B.
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make public comments on items within the subject matter jurisdiction of the council/agency board that are not listed on this agenda or are listed on this agenda as an item other than a public hearing item. Members of the audience will have the opportunity to address the
city council/agency board about public hearing items at the time the public hearing is held. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the council/agency board is prohibited from taking action on oral requests, but may refer the matter to staff or to a subsequent meeting. The council/agency board will respond after public comment has been received. Each person or representative of a group shall be allowed to speak without interruption for up to five (5) continuous minutes, subject to compliance with applicable meeting rules. Questions to the speaker or responses to the speaker's questions or comments shall be handled after the speaker has completed his/her comments. Public Participation will be limited to sixty (60) minutes.
C.
REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL
1.
Mayor Rocha: Request for a $200.00 donation to Lee School to assist with costs associated with bus transportation for 86 to 100 4th grade students to visit Mission San Juan Capistrano on April 27, 2016.
2.
Mayor Rocha: Request for a Proclamation proclaiming the month of May, 2016 as â€œLupus Awareness Monthâ€ in the City of Azusa for Looms4Lupus, a non-profit organization.
C-2 Lupus Awareness Month Proclamation
3.
City Manager: Request for a Proclamation proclaiming the week of May 1-7, 2016 as Public Service Recognition Week in the City of Azusa.
C-3 Public Service Recognition Week Proclamation
4.
City Clerk: Request for a Proclamation proclaiming the week of May 1-7, 2016 as the 47th Annual Municipal Clerks Week in the City of Azusa.
C-4 Municipal Clerks Week Proclamation
D.
CONSENT CALENDAR
The Consent Calendar adopting the printed recommended actions will be enacted with one vote. If Councilmembers or Staff wish to address any item on the Consent Calendar
individually, it will be considered under SPECIAL CALL ITEMS.
1.
MINUTES OF THE ADJOURNED REGULAR/SPECIAL MEETING OF FEBRUARY 22, 2016 AND THE REGULAR MEETING OF MARCH 7, 2016.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve minutes as written.
D-1 Minutes Adj Regular-Special Mtg 2-22-16
D-1 Minutes Reg Mtg 3-7-16
2.
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING PAYMENTS OF WARRANTS BY THE CITY.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution No. 2016-C28 allowing certain claims and demands and specifying the funds out of which the same are to be paid.
D-2 Warrant Register Res. No. 2016-C28
3.
HUMAN RESOURCES ACTION ITEMS.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the Personnel Action Requests in accordance with the City of Azusa Civil Service Rules and applicable Memorandum of Understanding(s).
D-3 Staff Report - Human Resources Action Items
4.
REQUEST TO APPROVE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH THINKNOW RESEARCH FOR PUBLIC OPINION RESEARCH SURVEY.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve a Professional Services Agreement with ThinkNow Research to conduct a Public Opinion Research Survey in an amount not to exceed $25,000, and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the City.
D-4 Staff Report - Agreement with ThinkNow Research
5.
REQUEST TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2016-C29 AUTHORIZING SUBMITTAL OF APPLICATION FOR CALRECYCLE PAYMENT PROGRAMS AND RELATED AUTHORIZATIONS.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution No. 2016-C29 authorizing submittal of application for CalRecycle payment programs and related authorizations.
D-5 Staff Report -CalRecycle Payment Programs
6.
PURCHASE OF 500 KCMIL UNDERGROUND COPPER CABLE.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the issuance of a purchase order to One Source Supply in an amount not to exceed $92,930.13.
D-6 Staff Report - Purchase of 500KCML Copper Cable
7.
AWARD OF CONTRACT TO CLEAN ABOVE THE CEILING TILES AT CITY HALL WEST WING.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Award a contract to Western Indoor Environmental Services to clean above the ceiling tiles at City Hall West Wing in an amount not to exceed $58,025, and authorize the City Manager to execute a contract, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the City.
D-7 Staff Report - West Wing Above Ceiling Tiles Decontamination
8.
APPROVE AMENDMENT TO LETTER AGREEMENT WITH MUNITEMPS FOR INTERIM ASSISTANT CITY CLERK SERVICES.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve an amendment to the Letter Agreement with MuniTemps for Interim Assistant City Clerk services increasing the total compensation by an additional $14,000 for a not-to-exceed amount of $64,000, and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the City.
D-8 Staff Report - Agreement with MuniTemps
E.
ADJOURNMENT
UPCOMING MEETINGS:
May 2, 2016, 6:30 p.m. Ceremonial/Closed Session, 7:30 p.m. Regular Meeting
May 16, 2016, 6:30 p.m. Ceremonial/Closed Session, 7:30 p.m. Regular Meeting
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in a city meeting, please contact the City Clerk at 626-812-5229. Notification three (3) working days prior to the meeting when special services are needed will assist staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide access to the meeting.
minutes_text:
CITY OF AZUSA
  MINUTES OF THE CITY COUNCIL AND
  THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE
  FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
  REGULAR MEETING
  MONDAY, APRIL 18, 2016 – 6:30 P.M.

The City Council of the City of Azusa met in regular session at the above date and time in the Azusa Auditorium
located at 213 E. Foothill Boulevard, Azusa, CA 91702.

Mayor Rocha called the meeting to order at 6:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo.
Staff Members: City Manager Butzlaff, City Attorney Martinez, Neighborhood Services Coordinator Quiroz,
Administrative Technician Juarez.

CLOSED SESSION

The City Council recessed to Closed Session at 6:32 P.M. to discuss the following:

1. CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS – Pursuant to California Government Code,
  Section 54956.8.
  Property Address:  340 N. Orange Avenue (Azusa Armory)
  Agency Negotiators:  Troy Butzlaff, City Manager
  Negotiating Parties: Daniel C. Kim, California Director of General Services
  Under Negotiation:  Price and Terms of Sale

2. CONFERENCE INVOLVING A JOINT POWERS AUTHORITY – EAST SAN GABRIEL VALLEY
  CONSORTIUM dba L.A. WORKS – Pursuant to California Government Code 54956.96.
  Discussion will concern: Exposure to Litigation
  Azusa Agency Representatives: Joe Rocha, Mayor; Troy Butzlaff, City Manager

3. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATIONS – Pursuant to California Government Code,
  Section 54957.
  Titles: City Manager and City Attorney

The City Council reconvened at 7:30 P.M.; City Attorney Martinez announced the following regarding Closed Session:
Item 1: Council provided direction to City negotiator, no other reportable action; Item 2: No reportable action; and Item
3: Council will continue to conduct the evaluations, item will be on future agendas.

REGULAR SESSION

Mayor Rocha called the meeting to order at 7:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo, City Treasurer Vasquez
Staff Members: City Manager Butzlaff, City Attorney Martinez, Director of Human Resources and Risk Management
Ayala, Director of Economic and Community Development Christiansen, Public Works Director/City Engineer
Bobadilla, Police Chief Gonzalez, Utilities Director Morrow, Interim Finance Director Johnson, Management Analyst
Lacasella, Neighborhood Services Coordinator Quiroz, Administrative Technician Juarez.
 The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mr. Jeff Cameron.

The invocation was given by Pastor Ariel Verayo, Jesus is Lord Church.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Mr. Dan Simpson expressed his desire for the re-opening of the Garcia Trail and inquired about its restoration.

Mr. Hector Elizalde provided information regarding the 5th Veteran’s Forum scheduled to take place on June 25, 2016 at
the National Guard Armory and discussed the Department of Veterans Affairs.

Mr. Raphael Olano commented on the recently posted parking restrictions located in the areas surrounding the
Downtown Gold Line Station.

City Manager Butzlaff responded that he would prepare answers to the questions posed by Mr. Simpson to be provided
at a later time. With respect to restricted parkinghe encouraged residents to utilize Azusa Transit to shuttle back and
forth from the stations. He announced a Special City Council meeting on April 25th following the Utility Board meeting
to discuss issues related to parking.

REPORTS, UPDATES AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Butzlaff announced the annual City Hall clean-up on Friday, April 22.

Mayor Rocha: Request for a $200.00 donation to Lee School to assist with costs associated with bus transportation for
85 to 100 4th grade students to visit Mission San Juan Capistrano on April 27, 2016.

Moved by Councilmember Gonzales, seconded by Councilmember Alvarez, and carried by unanimous vote of the
members present to approve a donation to Lee School.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

Mayor Rocha: Request for a Proclamation proclaiming the month of May, 2016 as “Lupus Awareness Month” in the
City of Azusa for Looms4Lupus, a non-profit organization.

Moved by Mayor Pro-Tem Carrillo, seconded by Councilmember Gonzales, and carried by unanimous vote of the
members present to approve a proclamation proclaiming the month of May 2016 as “Lupus Awareness Month.”

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

City Manager: Request for a Proclamation proclaiming the week of May 1-7, 2016 as Public Service Recognition Week
in the City of Azusa.

Moved by Mayor Pro-Tem Carrillo, seconded by Councilmember Macias, and carried by unanimous vote of the
members present to approve a proclamation proclaiming the week of May 1-7, 2016 as Public Service Recognition
Week.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

City Clerk: Request for a Proclamation proclaiming the week of May 1-7, 2016 as the 47th Annual Municipal Clerks
Week in the City of Azusa.

Moved by Councilmember Gonzales, seconded by Councilmember Macias, and carried by unanimous vote of the
members present to approve a proclamation proclaiming the week of May 1-7, 2016 as the 47th Annual Municipal
Clerks Week in the City of Azusa.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

Councilmember Macias discussed the issues related to the Department of Veterans Affairs, offered his condolences in
the passing of WWII Veteran, Mr. Jim Rose, and reminded everyone that Fish Canyon Falls was open to hikers.

Councilmember Alvarez suggested that a session regarding veteran burials be added to the Annual Veteran’s Forum.

Councilmember Gonzales thanked City Staff for their recognition of Earth Day throughout the month of April. He
announced the Shred-a-Thon on Saturday, April 23 at Azusa Light & Water, and recognized the Armenian Genocide as
well as all other Genocides.

4/18/2016 – PAGE TWO
 Mayor Rocha announced that the meeting would be adjourned in memory of Mr. Rodolfo Salgado Ramirez and Ms.
Frances Villanueva Salce, lifelong Azusa residents, and Mr. Jim Rose, WWII Veteran and longtime Azusa resident. He
announced the following events: April 21 - Arbor Day; April 22 - Azusa Reads, Writes and Counts; April 23 – Azusa
Unified School District’s Parent University; April 24 - Remembrance Day in honor of the Armenian Genocide; and
April 24 - Relay for Life.

CONSENT CALENDAR: Moved by Councilmember Gonzales, seconded by Mayor Pro-Tem Carrillo, to approve
Consent Calendar Items D-1 to D-8, and carried by the following vote of the Council:

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

1. The minutes of the Adjourned Regular/Special Meeting of February 22, 2016 and the Regular Meeting of March 7,
  2016 were approved as written.

2. Resolution No. 2016-C28 was adopted and entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND
  DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID.

3. The Human Resources Action Items, in accordance with the City of Azusa Civil Service Rules and applicable
  Memorandum of Understanding(s), were approved as follows:
  Merit Increase and or Regular Appointments: C. Gutierrez, M. Shan Thompson
  Flexible Staffing Promotion: M. Vega
  Promotion: M. Barbosa, F. Cawte.

4. A Professional Services Agreement with ThinkNow Research to conduct a Public Opinion Research Survey in an
  amount not to exceed $25,000 was approved.

5. Resolution No. 2016-C29 was adopted and entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA, CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING
  SUBMITTAL OF APPLICATION TO THE DEPARTMENT OF RESOURCES RECYLCING AND RECOVERY
  (CALRECYCLE) FOR PAYMENT PROGRAMS AND RELATED AUTHORIZATIONS.

6. The issuance of a purchase order to One Source Supply in an amount not to exceed $92,930.13 was approved.

7. A contract was awarded to Western Indoor Environmental Services to clean above the ceiling tiles at City Hall West
  Wing in an amount not to exceed $58,025.

8. An amendment to the Letter Agreement with MuniTemps for Interim Assistant City Clerk services increasing the
  total compensation by an additional $14,000 for a not-to-exceed amount of $64,000 was approved.

ADJOURNMENT:

The meeting was adjourned by consensus of the City Council in memory of Mr. Rodolfo Salgado Ramirez and Ms.
Frances Villanueva Salce, lifelong Azusa residents, and Mr. Jim Rose, WWII veteran and longtime Azusa resident.

TIME OF ADJOURNMENT: 8:14 P.M.

_________________________________
CITY CLERK
